sections.description:
Secure WordPress MCP Server for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Gemini & Other AI Agents

WordPress MCP server built for security: miniOrange Secure MCP Server connects Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Cursor, Claude Code and any MCP client to your site through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Each team member connects their own AI agent, limited to their WordPress role. Every tool call is checked, logged and reversible.

It is the WordPress MCP server built for teams and agencies: 772 MCP tools for WordPress and 45+ popular plugins (518 free, 254 Pro), OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, role-based access, human approval, data loss prevention (DLP) and a full audit log. Connect Claude to WordPress or connect ChatGPT to WordPress in about 2 minutes.

Ask your AI agent to write and publish blog posts, edit Elementor and Kadence layouts block by block, manage custom post types and ACF fields, update WooCommerce products, edit Yoast SEO and Rank Math fields, moderate comments, manage users and handle form entries. You decide which tools each AI agent can use.

Quick Links

Official Website | ChatGPT Setup Guide | Claude Setup Guide | All Setup Guides | Documentation | Book a Demo

What is an MCP server for WordPress?

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that lets AI assistants call tools on other systems. An MCP server for WordPress exposes your site’s actions (create a post, update a product, change a menu) as tools that an AI client such as Claude or ChatGPT can call.

Without guardrails, an AI agent connected to WordPress can do anything its account can do. Secure MCP Server adds the controls a team needs: per-user identity, per-role tool limits, approvals for risky actions, sensitive-data masking and an audit trail of every call.

Key features of the secure WordPress MCP server

  • Every user connects their own AI – each person uses their own ChatGPT or Claude, limited to the tools you allow their role.
  • 518 MCP tools in 36 categories – WordPress core, the block editor, menus and widgets, WooCommerce, Yoast SEO, Rank Math, Advanced Custom Fields, Elementor, Kadence, Contact Form 7, WPForms, Gravity Forms, Fluent Forms, Wordfence, UpdraftPlus and more.
  • Role-based MCP adapter – abilities that other plugins register appear in the Agent Registry, ready to grant per role.
  • Block-by-block page editing – AI changes one heading, paragraph or button and leaves the rest of the page exactly as it was.
  • Changes show straight away – page caches are cleared automatically after every AI change, and drafts can be shared with an expiring preview link.
  • Governed REST API access – AI can use any WordPress REST endpoint, including those from your other plugins, with route-by-route, role-based permissions.
  • Agent Registry – decide, per WordPress role, exactly which tools an AI agent can use.
  • Self-hosted OAuth 2.1 with PKCE – the AI never sees your WordPress password.
  • Every call checked against WordPress capabilities – an AI can never do more than its user can do in wp-admin.
  • Full audit log – every call, allowed or refused, is recorded.
  • Safe theme and code editing – changes go to a draft, are syntax-checked and previewed, and publish with automatic backup and rollback.
  • Built-in troubleshooting – a Troubleshooting page finds out why an AI client can’t connect and tells you what to fix.

How to Install the WordPress MCP Server

Install and create your first AI agent

  1. In your WordPress admin, go to Plugins → Add New, search for Secure MCP Server, then click Install Now and Activate.
  2. Open Secure MCP Server in the sidebar and click Register your first agent.
  3. Name the agent, choose which abilities each user role can use, then click Create & Continue.

How to Connect ChatGPT to WordPress

  1. Under Connect your AI client, choose ChatGPT and copy Your Site URL.
  2. Click the MCP Server for WordPress link to open the app in ChatGPT, then click Install Plugin.
  3. Paste your site URL, click Continue, then Allow Access.

Each team member connects their own ChatGPT the same way. Full guide: Connect ChatGPT to WordPress with MCP

Watch: connect ChatGPT to WordPress in 2 minutes

How to Connect Claude to WordPress

  1. Under Connect your AI client, choose Claude.
  2. Open the miniOrange MCP for WordPress connector and click Connect.
  3. Enter your site URL on the sign-in gateway, log in to WordPress and click Allow access.

Your approved tools now appear in Claude. Full guide: Connect Claude to WordPress with MCP

Watch: connect Claude to WordPress in 2 minutes

How to Connect Cursor to WordPress

Full guide: Connect Cursor to WordPress with MCP

Watch: connect Cursor to WordPress in 2 minutes

Connect Gemini, Windsurf, Antigravity, Grok & Any MCP Client

The Secure MCP Server plugin follows the open Model Context Protocol standard, so it works with Gemini, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, and any MCP-compatible client. Connect several AI clients at once, each with its own permissions and audit trail.

Your MCP server endpoint:
https://gateway.miniorange.ai/v2/mcp

What your WordPress AI agent can do: 772 MCP tools

Tools for a plugin appear only while that plugin is active.

Free – 518 tools (every plan)

  • Posts (31) and Pages (25) – create, update, duplicate, publish, schedule, unpublish, trash, restore and delete; set status, templates, featured images, categories and tags.
  • Categories (11), Tags (10) and Custom Content (19) – create, rename and delete terms; create and update custom post type items and custom fields.
  • Media (26) – upload from a URL or file, edit images, update alt text, titles and captions, find unattached media, and find images with missing thumbnail sizes or no alt text.
  • Revisions (9), Comments (21) and Content Editing (6) – restore revisions; approve, reply to, spam or delete comments; find and replace text across posts, fields and settings.
  • Block Editor (12) – insert, update, move, duplicate and delete Gutenberg blocks.
  • Users & Roles (38) – create, update and delete users, assign roles, reset passwords, update profiles.
  • Site Administration (73) – update site settings, activate and update plugins, check site health, clear caches, run cron events, manage menus, widgets, preview links and REST API routes.
  • Theme Editing (41) – edit block templates, global styles, patterns, theme files and custom CSS in a draft, then preview, publish or restore a backup.
  • Page Builders (30) – Elementor (12) and Kadence (18): read and write layouts, edit element content and styling, insert rows, columns and blocks.
  • WooCommerce (41) – create, update and delete products, orders, customers and coupons; change order status, add notes, issue refunds; sales and top-seller reports.
  • SEO (17) – Yoast SEO (14): update SEO titles, meta descriptions, focus keywords, canonicals, robots, schema and social cards. Rank Math (1) and read-only SEO data (2).
  • Advanced Custom Fields (25) – create field groups; get, update and bulk update fields, repeaters, flexible content and options pages.
  • Forms & Leads (54) – Contact Form 7 (with Flamingo), WPForms, Gravity Forms (40) and Fluent Forms (14): list, read, export as CSV and manage entries and notifications.
  • Security & Backups (29) – Wordfence (17): check protection, run scans and resolve findings, review attacks, traffic and failed logins, block or unblock IPs, and audit 2FA. UpdraftPlus (12): see backup history, start, cancel or delete backups, back up before a risky change, follow progress and logs, and change the schedule. Administrators only.

Pro – 254 more tools (Pro and Business plans)

  • Page Builders (75) – Elementor Pro (16) popups, Theme Builder and global styles; Divi (9), Divi 5 (13), WPBakery (7), Beaver Builder (7), Bricks (8), Oxygen (5), Breakdance (5) and Avada (5) layouts and elements.
  • Custom Fields (17) – ACF PRO (7), Meta Box (6), JetEngine (4).
  • SEO & Performance (27) – Rank Math Pro (8), All in One SEO (5), SEOPress (5), Yoast SEO Premium (5): redirects, schema, focus keywords, social meta. WP Rocket (4): clear and preload cache.
  • Multilingual (16) – WPML (7), Polylang (5), TranslatePress (4): create translations, set languages, update strings.
  • E-commerce & Subscriptions (36) – Easy Digital Downloads (7), WooCommerce Bookings (7), WooCommerce Subscriptions (9), Subscriptions for WooCommerce by WP Swings (7), WooCommerce Memberships (6).
  • Memberships (11) – MemberPress (6), Paid Memberships Pro (5).
  • Learning / LMS (26) – LearnDash (9), LifterLMS (5), Tutor LMS (12): create courses, lessons and quizzes, enroll students, track progress.
  • Events (10) – The Events Calendar (5), Events Calendar Pro (1), Event Tickets (4).
  • Forms (13) – Formidable Forms (5), Ninja Forms (4), Forminator (4).
  • Email Marketing & CRM (11) – FluentCRM (7), MailPoet (4).
  • Real Estate (8) – Houzez properties, agents and listing media.
  • Media (4) – find media used nowhere on the site and delete it, resize large images and set alt text in bulk.

Example prompts:

  • “Update the price of every product in the Winter category by 10%.”
  • “Rewrite the Yoast meta descriptions for our top 10 pages to under 155 characters.”
  • “Change the hero heading on the About page to ‘Built for teams’.”

MCP security: three layers on every call

  1. Identity – each AI agent signs in through OAuth 2.1 and acts as a specific WordPress user.
  2. Policy – the Agent Registry, per-tool toggles and WordPress capability checks decide what that agent may do.
  3. Monitoring – every call is logged, rate-limited and checked for prompt injection and unusual behavior.

Plus:

  • Confirmation before destructive actions.
  • Human approval for risky actions.
  • Sensitive data masking with data rules and DLP.
  • Undo AI changes within 72 hours.
  • Dashboard with active agents, executions, success rate and latency.

Need help?

Ask in the support forum – our team responds quickly. For private or enterprise questions, email aisupport@xecurify.com or use the Contact Support button inside the mcp server plugin.
sections.installation:
Requirements

  • WordPress 6.9 or newer (Abilities API required)
  • PHP 7.4 or higher (PHP 8.0+ recommended)
  • HTTPS enabled (for OAuth login)

From your WordPress dashboard

  1. Go to Plugins → Add New Plugin.
  2. Search for miniOrange Secure MCP Server.
  3. Click Install Now, then Activate.
  4. Open Secure MCP Server from the admin sidebar and click Register your first agent.
  5. Name the agent, set ability access by user role, and click Create & Continue.
  6. Under Connect your AI client, choose Claude, ChatGPT or another client and follow the setup panel.
  7. Sign in to WordPress and click Allow Access. Done!

Manual installation

  1. Download the plugin zip.
  2. Go to Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin and upload the zip.
  3. Activate the plugin and continue from step 4 above.
sections.faq:
What is an MCP server for WordPress?

It is a plugin that exposes your WordPress site’s actions as Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, so AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT can manage your site through chat.

Can I limit what an editor’s AI can do?

Yes. Use the Agent Registry to choose which tools each role can use, and turn off any individual tool.

Is it safe to give AI access to my WordPress site?

Yes. Access uses self-hosted OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, so the AI never sees your password. Every call is limited by role through the agent Registry, checked against WordPress capabilities, rate-limited and logged. You can require human approval for sensitive actions and mask sensitive data. Rate limits are enforced by the miniOrange Gateway; human approval and data masking are part of the Business plan.

Which AI clients are supported?

Claude (Claude.ai, Claude Desktop and Claude Code), ChatGPT, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, Windsurf, Grok and any MCP client that supports remote MCP servers.

How do I connect ChatGPT to WordPress?

Register an agent, choose ChatGPT under Connect your AI client, open the MCP Server for WordPress app in ChatGPT, paste your site URL and click Allow Access.

Can AI break my theme or site?

Theme and code edits happen in a draft copy first, with a backup and rollback. You can also undo supported AI changes.

Does it work with WooCommerce?

Yes. 41 free WooCommerce tools cover products, stock, prices, orders, customers and coupons.

Can I connect multiple AI clients?

Yes. You can connect several clients and agents, and revoke any of them at any time.

How do I revoke access?

Open AI Agents in Secure MCP Server, open the agent and switch it off, or delete it. The connection stops working immediately.

What happens if an AI edit goes wrong?

Check the audit log to see exactly what changed, then restore from the revision, the theme backup or the Undo feature.

description:
Secure WordPress MCP Server for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Gemini & Other AI Agents

WordPress MCP server built for security: miniOrange Secure MCP Server connects Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Cursor, Claude Code and any MCP client to your site through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Each team member connects their own AI agent, limited to their WordPress role. Every tool call is checked, logged and reversible.

It is the WordPress MCP server built for teams and agencies: 772 MCP tools for WordPress and 45+ popular plugins (518 free, 254 Pro), OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, role-based access, human approval, data loss prevention (DLP) and a full audit log. Connect Claude to WordPress or connect ChatGPT to WordPress in about 2 minutes.

Ask your AI agent to write and publish blog posts, edit Elementor and Kadence layouts block by block, manage custom post types and ACF fields, update WooCommerce products, edit Yoast SEO and Rank Math fields, moderate comments, manage users and handle form entries. You decide which tools each AI agent can use.

Quick Links

Official Website | ChatGPT Setup Guide | Claude Setup Guide | All Setup Guides | Documentation | Book a Demo

What is an MCP server for WordPress?

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that lets AI assistants call tools on other systems. An MCP server for WordPress exposes your site’s actions (create a post, update a product, change a menu) as tools that an AI client such as Claude or ChatGPT can call.

Without guardrails, an AI agent connected to WordPress can do anything its account can do. Secure MCP Server adds the controls a team needs: per-user identity, per-role tool limits, approvals for risky actions, sensitive-data masking and an audit trail of every call.

Key features of the secure WordPress MCP server

  • Every user connects their own AI – each person uses their own ChatGPT or Claude, limited to the tools you allow their role.
  • 518 MCP tools in 36 categories – WordPress core, the block editor, menus and widgets, WooCommerce, Yoast SEO, Rank Math, Advanced Custom Fields, Elementor, Kadence, Contact Form 7, WPForms, Gravity Forms, Fluent Forms, Wordfence, UpdraftPlus and more.
  • Role-based MCP adapter – abilities that other plugins register appear in the Agent Registry, ready to grant per role.
  • Block-by-block page editing – AI changes one heading, paragraph or button and leaves the rest of the page exactly as it was.
  • Changes show straight away – page caches are cleared automatically after every AI change, and drafts can be shared with an expiring preview link.
  • Governed REST API access – AI can use any WordPress REST endpoint, including those from your other plugins, with route-by-route, role-based permissions.
  • Agent Registry – decide, per WordPress role, exactly which tools an AI agent can use.
  • Self-hosted OAuth 2.1 with PKCE – the AI never sees your WordPress password.
  • Every call checked against WordPress capabilities – an AI can never do more than its user can do in wp-admin.
  • Full audit log – every call, allowed or refused, is recorded.
  • Safe theme and code editing – changes go to a draft, are syntax-checked and previewed, and publish with automatic backup and rollback.
  • Built-in troubleshooting – a Troubleshooting page finds out why an AI client can’t connect and tells you what to fix.

How to Install the WordPress MCP Server

Install and create your first AI agent

  1. In your WordPress admin, go to Plugins → Add New, search for Secure MCP Server, then click Install Now and Activate.
  2. Open Secure MCP Server in the sidebar and click Register your first agent.
  3. Name the agent, choose which abilities each user role can use, then click Create & Continue.

How to Connect ChatGPT to WordPress

  1. Under Connect your AI client, choose ChatGPT and copy Your Site URL.
  2. Click the MCP Server for WordPress link to open the app in ChatGPT, then click Install Plugin.
  3. Paste your site URL, click Continue, then Allow Access.

Each team member connects their own ChatGPT the same way. Full guide: Connect ChatGPT to WordPress with MCP

Watch: connect ChatGPT to WordPress in 2 minutes

How to Connect Claude to WordPress

  1. Under Connect your AI client, choose Claude.
  2. Open the miniOrange MCP for WordPress connector and click Connect.
  3. Enter your site URL on the sign-in gateway, log in to WordPress and click Allow access.

Your approved tools now appear in Claude. Full guide: Connect Claude to WordPress with MCP

Watch: connect Claude to WordPress in 2 minutes

How to Connect Cursor to WordPress

Full guide: Connect Cursor to WordPress with MCP

Watch: connect Cursor to WordPress in 2 minutes

Connect Gemini, Windsurf, Antigravity, Grok & Any MCP Client

The Secure MCP Server plugin follows the open Model Context Protocol standard, so it works with Gemini, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, and any MCP-compatible client. Connect several AI clients at once, each with its own permissions and audit trail.

Your MCP server endpoint:
https://gateway.miniorange.ai/v2/mcp

What your WordPress AI agent can do: 772 MCP tools

Tools for a plugin appear only while that plugin is active.

Free – 518 tools (every plan)

  • Posts (31) and Pages (25) – create, update, duplicate, publish, schedule, unpublish, trash, restore and delete; set status, templates, featured images, categories and tags.
  • Categories (11), Tags (10) and Custom Content (19) – create, rename and delete terms; create and update custom post type items and custom fields.
  • Media (26) – upload from a URL or file, edit images, update alt text, titles and captions, find unattached media, and find images with missing thumbnail sizes or no alt text.
  • Revisions (9), Comments (21) and Content Editing (6) – restore revisions; approve, reply to, spam or delete comments; find and replace text across posts, fields and settings.
  • Block Editor (12) – insert, update, move, duplicate and delete Gutenberg blocks.
  • Users & Roles (38) – create, update and delete users, assign roles, reset passwords, update profiles.
  • Site Administration (73) – update site settings, activate and update plugins, check site health, clear caches, run cron events, manage menus, widgets, preview links and REST API routes.
  • Theme Editing (41) – edit block templates, global styles, patterns, theme files and custom CSS in a draft, then preview, publish or restore a backup.
  • Page Builders (30) – Elementor (12) and Kadence (18): read and write layouts, edit element content and styling, insert rows, columns and blocks.
  • WooCommerce (41) – create, update and delete products, orders, customers and coupons; change order status, add notes, issue refunds; sales and top-seller reports.
  • SEO (17) – Yoast SEO (14): update SEO titles, meta descriptions, focus keywords, canonicals, robots, schema and social cards. Rank Math (1) and read-only SEO data (2).
  • Advanced Custom Fields (25) – create field groups; get, update and bulk update fields, repeaters, flexible content and options pages.
  • Forms & Leads (54) – Contact Form 7 (with Flamingo), WPForms, Gravity Forms (40) and Fluent Forms (14): list, read, export as CSV and manage entries and notifications.
  • Security & Backups (29) – Wordfence (17): check protection, run scans and resolve findings, review attacks, traffic and failed logins, block or unblock IPs, and audit 2FA. UpdraftPlus (12): see backup history, start, cancel or delete backups, back up before a risky change, follow progress and logs, and change the schedule. Administrators only.

Pro – 254 more tools (Pro and Business plans)

  • Page Builders (75) – Elementor Pro (16) popups, Theme Builder and global styles; Divi (9), Divi 5 (13), WPBakery (7), Beaver Builder (7), Bricks (8), Oxygen (5), Breakdance (5) and Avada (5) layouts and elements.
  • Custom Fields (17) – ACF PRO (7), Meta Box (6), JetEngine (4).
  • SEO & Performance (27) – Rank Math Pro (8), All in One SEO (5), SEOPress (5), Yoast SEO Premium (5): redirects, schema, focus keywords, social meta. WP Rocket (4): clear and preload cache.
  • Multilingual (16) – WPML (7), Polylang (5), TranslatePress (4): create translations, set languages, update strings.
  • E-commerce & Subscriptions (36) – Easy Digital Downloads (7), WooCommerce Bookings (7), WooCommerce Subscriptions (9), Subscriptions for WooCommerce by WP Swings (7), WooCommerce Memberships (6).
  • Memberships (11) – MemberPress (6), Paid Memberships Pro (5).
  • Learning / LMS (26) – LearnDash (9), LifterLMS (5), Tutor LMS (12): create courses, lessons and quizzes, enroll students, track progress.
  • Events (10) – The Events Calendar (5), Events Calendar Pro (1), Event Tickets (4).
  • Forms (13) – Formidable Forms (5), Ninja Forms (4), Forminator (4).
  • Email Marketing & CRM (11) – FluentCRM (7), MailPoet (4).
  • Real Estate (8) – Houzez properties, agents and listing media.
  • Media (4) – find media used nowhere on the site and delete it, resize large images and set alt text in bulk.

Example prompts:

  • “Update the price of every product in the Winter category by 10%.”
  • “Rewrite the Yoast meta descriptions for our top 10 pages to under 155 characters.”
  • “Change the hero heading on the About page to ‘Built for teams’.”

MCP security: three layers on every call

  1. Identity – each AI agent signs in through OAuth 2.1 and acts as a specific WordPress user.
  2. Policy – the Agent Registry, per-tool toggles and WordPress capability checks decide what that agent may do.
  3. Monitoring – every call is logged, rate-limited and checked for prompt injection and unusual behavior.

Plus:

  • Confirmation before destructive actions.
  • Human approval for risky actions.
  • Sensitive data masking with data rules and DLP.
  • Undo AI changes within 72 hours.
  • Dashboard with active agents, executions, success rate and latency.

Need help?

Ask in the support forum – our team responds quickly. For private or enterprise questions, email aisupport@xecurify.com or use the Contact Support button inside the mcp server plugin.
